extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, respondents in USPTO disciplinary proceedings, OED staff, and counsel handling reciprocal discipline matters
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards governing the imposition of reciprocal discipline by the USPTO under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 when a practitioner has been disciplined (e.g., disbarred) by a state authority. Includes notice, opportunity to respond, scope of record, sanctions ordered, and post-order obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the USPTO may impose reciprocal discipline identical to the discipline imposed by a duly constituted authority of a State, pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 and 35 U.S.C. § 32.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure: OED files a Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline and mails a 'Notice and Order Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24' by certified mail. The Notice provides an opportunity to file a response opposing identical reciprocal discipline within forty (40) days, based on the reasons set forth in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1). Reciprocal matters at this stage have a limited record and no opportunity for discovery (see 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(b)). Requests for extensions may be granted; but failure to respond can lead to imposition of reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)
rubrics_metrics.description: A violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h) is predicated upon being disbarred on consent from the practice of law by a duly constituted authority of a State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: respondent signed an Affidavit of Surrender and was disbarred by Consent Order in state court; that disbarment serves as the predicate for the § 11.804(h) violation and USPTO reciprocal action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and service requirements (certified mail and delivery)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order must be mailed by certified mail and delivery is required (the document cites certified mail receipt numbers and delivery dates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The record should show mailing by certified mail and successful delivery; the Notice's delivery triggers the respondent's 40-day response window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to oppose based on 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent may oppose imposition of identical reciprocal discipline within the prescribed time, based on one or more reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice must advise of the specific statutory grounds for opposition; if respondent fails to file a response within the time allowed (including any granted extensions), the Director may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited record and no discovery in reciprocal matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Reciprocal discipline proceedings at this stage have a limited record and there is no opportunity for discovery (referencing 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests in the nature of discovery will be denied. Extensions of time may be granted, but discovery requests are not permitted in these limited-record proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of failure to respond
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent does not file a response to the Notice and Order, the Director may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact and impose reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision here explicitly states Respondent did not respond despite receipt and extensions; that failure supported exclusion from practice before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of state-adjudicated misconduct as basis for USPTO discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Facts established in the state disciplinary proceeding may be used as the basis for USPTO discipline (e.g., mishandling client funds: respondent received approximately $16,000 assigned to a third party and used funds without third party authorization, violating state rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order cites the state rules violated (North Carolina Rules of Professional Conduct Rules 1.15-20) and 8.4(c) as the misconduct underlying the state disbarment; those findings support USPTO reciprocal action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific sanction: exclusion from practice before the USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary sanction ordered is exclusion from the practice of patent, trademark, and non-patent law before the USPTO effective the date of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reciprocal discipline is imposed identical to the state-imposed discipline; exclusion prevents practice before the USPTO until reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Notice in the Official Gazette and OED Reading Room
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must publish a Notice of Exclusion in the Official Gazette and the disciplinary decisions are posted in the OED Reading Room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice must identify the respondent, registration number, the basis for discipline (e.g., violating 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h) predicated on state disbarment), and summarize the misconduct (e.g., facts about misappropriated funds).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to state disciplinary agencies and courts per 37 C.F.R. § 11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in states where the respondent is admitted, to courts where the respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures other jurisdictions and courts are informed of the USPTO's reciprocal discipline and the underlying reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the order does not reproduce § 11.58, it imposes the respondent's obligations under that regulation (e.g., obligations following discipline such as notification duties).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from USPTO Customer Numbers and PKI certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO will dissociate the respondent's name from any Customer Numbers and the public key infrastructure (PKI) certificate associated with those Customer Numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents the respondent from using prior electronic credentials to practice before the USPTO while excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on obtaining or being added to a USPTO Customer Number until reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not apply for a USPTO Customer Number, obtain a USPTO Customer Number, nor have his name added to a USPTO Customer Number unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit post-discipline restriction tied to the respondent's exclusion; reinstatement is required before any Customer Number privileges can be restored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory authority for action
rubrics_metrics.description: The disciplinary action is taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citing the statutory and regulatory basis situates the authority for reciprocal discipline and publication/notification duties.
